{"sha":"da7b293644b08e767271744be63775491cd553ba","html_url":"https://github.com/AI-Riksarkivet/rask/commit/da7b293644b08e767271744be63775491cd553ba","commit":{"author":{"name":"Borg93","email":"Borg93@users.noreply.github.com","date":"2026-10-24T05:40:52Z"},"committer":{"name":"Borg93","email":"Borg93@users.noreply.github.com","date":"2026-10-24T05:40:52Z"},"message":"fix(lineage,chart): LH-533 — lineage's bus subscription delivers in parallel, at most 64 unacknowledged, and a commit refuses an event of a run another author bound

Read back live on rev 9 (afa32f06), lineage's group commit never took more than one event: 61 of 61 deliveries ran back
to back. Dapr's JetStream component hands its app one message at a time unless its metadata names a `concurrencyMode`
(components-contrib v1.19.0, `pubsub/jetstream/metadata.go:63-65`), and lineage's named none. In criterion 5's
catalog-kill drill the one delivery the kill failed took the sidecar's 120 s retry and held 21 later events behind it;
the backlog drained 171 s after the kill, inside the drill's 300 s.

Owner, 2026-10-24: parallel delivery with a commit-time author check, bounded by `maxAckPending: 64`.

- Lineage's subscriber component says `concurrencyMode: parallel` and `maxAckPending` from the new value
  `services.lineage.deliveriesInFlight` (64); the other subscribers keep one at a time. A sidecar cannot rebind a durable
  whose config changed, so the NATS stream Job recreates `lineage-durable` when its `max_ack_pending` differs and checks
  again until a sidecar has recreated it at the bound (the outgoing pod's may recreate it as it was); the recreated
  durable replays the retained stream into the keyed ingest.
- Events delivered together are each authorized before any of them binds its run, so `ProvenanceStore._commit` asks the
  doors' rule again where the doors ask it (`refuse_foreign_runs`, from `fga_enabled`): a run is bound to its first
  event's author, the table's binding or else the batch's first, and an event of it naming another author is refused
  with none of its rows written. The bus door acks that refusal as unrepairable, and the HTTP door counts it as its own.
- The two integration tests deliver through the bus door's handler over the real store and catalog.

Red checks, in a snapshot worktree over the lineage scope (716 tests): the author check off, the bus door's arm for it
removed, and the last event binding a run each redden the burst test alone; no split and the feed rows before the edges
redden the refusal test alone; no dedupe reddens the burst test alone. The Job's convergence runs against a real NATS
only, and is read back on the deploy.
